title: Operator onboarding knowledge rot and automation impact
author: Elena Rivera
body:
Summary

This retrospective analyzes a six-month pattern of knowledge decay in the Platform Operator on-call cohort ("operators") and the measurable impact of two concurrent automation projects (prefetch-safety automation and alert-routing automation) on incident resolution time. The goal is to capture root causes for operator knowledge rot, quantify operational risk introduced by fast automation rollouts, and propose low-friction fixes to onboarding, runbook hygiene, and automation design.

Background and context

- Timeline: July 2025 — December 2025
- Scope: Platform operator team supporting multi-tenant LLM inference surface (regional schedulers, KV prefix cache, tenant burst credit system, and emergency model swap playbooks).
- Triggering event: A two-hour elevated-severity degradation on 2025-11-18 that required a manual cache re-shard and an operator-led model variant swap. Post-incident audit flagged repeated instances where junior operators lacked procedural recall for partial KV rebalancing and had to escalate to senior engineers.

Why this matters

- High cognitive load and uneven exposure to edge-case operational procedures increases mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for non-standard degradations.
- Automation without clear operator-centered rollback semantics led to situations where the automation masked symptoms, degrading observability.

Timeline of observations

1. July–Aug 2025: Two automation projects launched in beta (prefetch-safety automation, alert-routing automation).
2. Sep 2025: Onboarding class size increases (3 new operators) and time-in-role distribution skews younger (median tenure drops from 18m to 8m).
3. Oct–Nov 2025: Three incidents show repeated manual intervention patterns for partial KV re-shard. Time-to-first-action trended up (see metrics).
4. 2025-11-18: Elevated-severity incident — operator escalated to runtime team; incident revealed gaps in runbook clarity and missing telemetry links.
5. Dec 2025: Triage project commissioned to audit runbooks and automation semantics.

Key findings

- Quantitative:
  - Median MTTM for incidents involving KV-cache rebalancing increased from 18m (H1 2025) to 37m (Jul–Nov 2025).
  - Incidents where automation was active had 1.4x longer diagnostics time on average.
  - 58% of junior operators could not recall the canonical partial re-shard checklist during an on-call drill.

- Qualitative:
  - Runbooks had grown organically: duplication, outdated commands, and unclear decision gates (e.g., when to trigger manual re-shard vs. rely on automation).
  - Automation projects lacked a consistent operator-facing operational contract (expected states, safe-fail behavior, observable signals).
  - Knowledge distribution relied too heavily on tribal knowledge and war-room-style handoffs.

Root causes

1. Onboarding curriculum drift: training materials did not reflect recent automation changes; drills were not updated.
2. Runbook entropy: no enforced schema or linting for runbooks; runbooks contained copy/paste blocks with conflicting thresholds.
3. Insufficient automation contracts: teams delivering automation focused on correctness but not operator ergonomics (rollbacks, shadow-mode signals).
4. Sparse live practice: operators rarely exercised partial re-shards in low-risk labs; synthetic exercises focused on full-fail scenarios.

Actions taken during triage (Dec 2025–Jan 2026)

- Immediate:
  - Created a "partial-kv-rebalance" quick-play runbook excerpt and pinned to on-call Slack channel (owner: Kai Thompson).
  - Disabled prefetch-safety automation in two low-traffic regions to improve signal clarity for operators during drills.
  - Rewrote alert-routing automation to emit a structured "automation-state" event that surfaces to the incident timeline pipeline.

- Medium-term (30–90 days):
  - Runbook schema adoption: established a minimal metadata header (intent, preconditions, safe-fail points, rollbacks, test command).
  - Onboarding refresh: added a mandatory 4-hour lab for partial KV re-shard, with certification checklist and paired drills.
  - Automation contract template: introduced a 1-page operator contract required for any automation touching platform state.

Permanent changes and roadmap items

We decided on a set of permanent actions prioritized by risk reduction and operational cost. These items are tracked in the platform roadmap and quarter planning. Owners and target milestones are listed below.

- Runbook Governance (Owner: Platform Docs Core — lead: Priya Shah) — Q1 2026
  - Enforce a runbook linter in CI for docs in the canonical repo.
  - Migrate high-use runbooks to a single-sourced, reviewed location with change approvals.

- Onboarding and Simulation (Owner: Operator Training — lead: Marcus Nguyen) — Q1–Q2 2026
  - Weekly scheduled micro-simulations (20–40 minute drills) for partial re-shard, tenant burst fairness incidents, and model swap flows.
  - Certification badge added to operator roster; renewal every 6 months.

- Automation Contract and Observability (Owner: Runtime Automation — lead: Aisha Patel) — Q1 2026
  - Automation must publish a structured event stream with states: START, PROGRESS, PAUSED, ROLLBACK_READY, COMPLETE, ERROR.
  - Add a standard taxonomy for automation observed metrics (latency, expected-impact, safe-fail-time).

- Dashboard and Alert changes (Owner: Observability — lead: Daniel Kim) — Q2 2026
  - New dashboard tile: "Automation overtakes operator signal" that highlights when automation has suppressed raw signals for >5m.
  - New alert: automation-unexpected-state (P2) that triggers operator review.

Operational runbook excerpt (canonical)

Title: partial-kv-rebalance (quick-play)
Intent: Rebalance a single KV prefix shard when eviction rates exceed 0.8 across a subset of pods.
Preconditions:
- Confirm target tenant slice and impacted shard id
- Confirm automation is not currently in ROLLBACK_READY or PROGRESS
Commands (example):
- Check current shard map: curl -s http://operator-api.internal/v1/shards | jq '.shards[] | select(.id=="shard-13")'
- Initiate manual rebalance: operator-cli rebalance --shard=shard-13 --mode=gradual --dry-run=false
- Monitor quick metrics: watch -n 10 "curl -s http://telemetry.internal/kv/metrics?shard=shard-13 | jq '.evictionRate,.getLatency'"
Decision gates:
1) If evictionRate falls <0.4 within 20 minutes, allow rebalance to complete.
2) If error state observed in operator-api or rebalance does not reduce evictionRate, trigger model-variant-swap runbook.
Rollbacks:
- operator-cli rebalance --rollback --shard=shard-13

Sample automation contract (minimal)

- name: prefetch-safety-guard
- owner: runtime-automation-team
- states: [START, PROGRESS, PAUSED, ROLLBACK_READY, COMPLETE, ERROR]
- visible_signals: [evictionRate, kvGetLatency, operatorLockHeld]
- safe_fails: auto-pause and emit ROLLBACK_READY when operatorLockHeld == true

Decision record table (summary)

| Decision | Owned by | Target date | Outcome |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Enforce runbook header schema and linter | Platform Docs Core | 2026-02-15 | Approved |
| Add automation-state events to incident timeline | Observability | 2026-01-28 | Implemented |
| Add partial-kv lab to onboarding | Operator Training | 2026-03-01 | In progress |

Metrics to track (success criteria)

- MTTM for KV-rebalance incidents reduces to <25m by end of Q2 2026.
- Automated incidents with active automation will have diagnostics time <= baseline (no automation) within 3 months of contract rollout.
- 90% of operators recertify partial-kv lab within 6 months of rollout.

Follow-ups and owners (next 90 days)

- Priya Shah: Runbook linter PR and migration plan (due 2026-02-15).
- Marcus Nguyen: Coordinate first 8 weeks of micro-simulations and publish schedule (due 2026-02-28).
- Aisha Patel: Automation contract template and a short SDK for emitting automation-state events (due 2026-02-10).
- Daniel Kim: Dashboard tile prototype and alert rule (due 2026-03-15).

Appendix A: On-call drill script (20 min)

1) 0–2m: Briefing — describe the synthetic partial-shard eviction event.
2) 2–6m: Operators examine dashboard and confirm automation-state events.
3) 6–12m: Execute partial-kv-rebalance quick-play. Engineer-in-loop monitors and injects a simulated error at 9m.
4) 12–18m: Execute rollback and model-variant-swap if decision gate met.
5) 18–20m: Debrief and note gaps in runbook wording and telemetry links.

Appendix B: Useful links and references

- Operator CLI docs: https://internal-docs.redwood.ai/operator-cli
- Canonical runbooks repo: git+ssh://git.internal/redwood/platform-runbooks.git
- Incident timeline pipeline docs: /eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/incident-signal-playbook-dashboard-library-2026

Acknowledgements

Thanks to the triage team (Kai Thompson, Aisha Patel, Marcus Nguyen, Priya Shah, Daniel Kim) and the on-call cohort for participating in drills and providing candid feedback.

This retrospective is intended to drive concrete changes to onboarding, runbook governance, and automation contracts. Please add comments inline in the canonical repo or contact the owners listed in the Follow-ups section.
